Its response contains two values you MUST read before collecting any user input: - isPriorityRestricted: if true, do NOT ask for priority and do NOT include the priority param. If false, ask the user: Low (10), Medium (11), High (12). - isDescrMandated: if true, description is mandatory - ask for it. If false, description is optional. These two values from getCaseAddSettings directly control which parameters you collect from the user and pass to this tool. You cannot correctly fill this form without calling getCaseAddSettings first. Then call listAllCategory to resolve categoryId. Collect subject and other applicable fields. Confirm before submitting. ATTACHMENTS: if the user attached files in this chat and wants them on the case, for EACH file call useChatFileInField with moduleName='HRCase' and the chat fileId from the [Attached files: ...] context; collect each response's fileId, fileName and fileSize and pass them in this tool's case_attachment parameter as a JSON array of objects - the returned fileId as filePath, plus fileName and fileSize. Max 5 files. NEVER pass raw chat fileIds into case_attachment. If the response returns status=Failure with a message about description being required or empty, ask the user to provide a description and resubmit. dependencyTools: getCaseAddSettings, listAllCategory, listCaseSubCategories, useChatFileInField

name: addLeaveType
summary: Creates a leave type: POST JSON whose root key is 'leavetype' containing the full configuration object.
description: Creates a leave type: POST JSON whose root key is 'leavetype' containing the full configuration object. LOW-FRICTION: Only 'name' must be collected first; if missing, ask once and show a minimal sample payload. Do not ask follow-up questions for other omitted fields. Never refuse with mandatory-field errors except for missing 'name'-merge SAFE DEFAULTS into a complete payload and POST. Users may override any field when they specify it (validityTo, description, credit rules, booking limits, duration flags, etc.). Never invent department, location, designation, role, or user IDs. SAFE DEFAULTS (apply each omitted field; user values win): - code: three uppercase letters from name (adjust last letter if collision risk). - type PAID; unit DAY; validityFrom: today yyyy-MM-dd. - applicable: Users {mode:1,list:['-1']}; Departments, Genders, Designations, Locations, Roles, MaritalStatus each {mode:1,list:[]} (all employees). - effectiveAfterUnit YEAR; effectiveAfterPeriod 0. - creditCount 12; creditFrequency YEARLY; resetFrequency YEARLY. - carryForward {enable:false,maxUnit:0}; encashment {enable:false,maxUnit:0}; exceedBalance {allow:false}. - weekendAsLeave -1; holidayAsLeave -1. - allowFullDay true; allowHalfDay true; allowQuarterDay false; allowHour false. - pastBooking {day:0}; futureBooking {day:0,applyBefore:0}; minLeave 0; maxLeave 0; fileUpload 0. APPLICABLE SHAPE: Seven keys (MaritalStatus, Departments, Genders, Designations, Locations, Roles, Users); each {mode: 1 include | 0 exclude, list: string ids}. list ['-1'] = all in that category; [] = none scoped. Resolve labels via getDepartmentDetails, getLocationDetails, getRecords. If lookup fails, revert that key to its safe default (empty list for that dimension), preserve other dimensions, note under Defaults applied, and do not block. AFTER SUCCESS (same turn, mandatory): fetchLeaveTypeDetails(newId). Present in order: (1) success line with name and id; (2) Defaults applied bullets for each auto-filled field (omit section if the user supplied every field); (3) readable summary from fetchLeaveTypeDetails grouped as Basics, Credit/Reset, Booking, Policy, Applicable (Users ['-1'] decodes to all users); (4) hint: editLeaveType. If fetchLeaveTypeDetails fails: still (1), (2), and the exact payload sent. Never end with only an id or raw JSON.

name: addOnDuty
summary: Submit an on-duty request for work outside office (client visits, meetings, events).
description: Submit an on-duty request for work outside office (client visits, meetings, events). Do not ask confirmation - proceed directly. Two modes based on unit param: Mode 1 (unit=0, day-based): dataObj per date has dayTaken (0=full, 1=half, 2=quarter) and session. Full day: no session. Half: session 1 or 2. Quarter: session 1-4. Default: full day. Mode 2 (unit=1, hours-based): dataObj per date has ftime/ttime in mins from midnight (09:00AM=540, 02:00PM=840). IMPORTANT - On-duty disambiguation (run this BEFORE step 0 whenever the user just says 'apply on-duty' / 'on-duty request' without explicitly choosing attendance OD vs an on-duty leave): a. Call getAttendanceSettingsMethods - Attendance On-Duty is available iff is_on_duty_enabled == true. b. Call getLeaveBalance for the same erecno - Leave-type On-Duty is available iff any entry in the leavetypes array has typeConstant == 'ON_DUTY' (equivalently type == 1). c. Route based on what is available: - Only Attendance OD available -> continue with this tool (addOnDuty) using the steps below. - Only Leave-type On-Duty available -> do NOT call this tool; hand off to applyLeave using that ON_DUTY leave type's leaveTypeId. - Both available -> ASK the user which one they want: 'Attendance on-duty request' or 'On-Duty leave'. Only after the user picks, proceed with the matching tool. - Neither available -> tell the user on-duty is not enabled for them and stop. Skip this disambiguation only when the user's wording already pins the path (e.g., 'attendance OD', 'OD request', 'client visit OD' -> this tool; 'apply on-duty leave', 'on-duty leave for ...' -> applyLeave). Before invoking (Attendance OD path): 0. Call getAttendanceSettingsMethods. Proceed only if is_on_duty_enabled is true; otherwise tell the user on-duty requests are disabled. 1. Call getAllODTypes. One type = use it. Multiple = fuzzy-match user input; ask only if no match. 2. Pick mode: from/to times -> unit=1, else unit=0 (default full day). 3. type='addData'. 4. startDate/endDate in dd-MMM-yyyy (same for single day). 5. dateFormat='dd-MMM-yyyy'. 6. dataObj: keys=date strings (dd-MMM-yyyy), values=mode-specific fields. 7. Pass desc only if user explicitly provides a reason. dependencyTools: getAttendanceSettingsMethods, getAllODTypes, getLeaveBalance

name: addRecord
summary: This action is used to add a record. It starts by retrieving the formlinkname using the identifyForm tool and then fetches the field details using the getFields tool, based on the formId obtained from identifyForm.
description: This action is used to add a record. It starts by retrieving the formlinkname using the identifyForm tool and then fetches the field details using the getFields tool, based on the formId obtained from identifyForm. The tool matches the user's input with the required fields and constructs the input using the RECORD_ADD_UPDATE PromptSection. STRICT: For Lookup fields, call getLookupOptions with the relevant labelname values in the fields parameter. The response contains lookupOptions where each field labelname maps to an array of { Value, Id } objects. Match the user's text against Value and send the corresponding Id. NEVER send display strings for Lookup fields. For Picklist and Dropdown fields, call getFieldOptions with the relevant labelname values to fetch available options. Match the user's input against the option values (case-sensitive). If an exact match is found, send the matched option value as-is. If no exact match is found, present the available options to the user and ask whether they want to choose from the existing options or quick-add the provided value as a new option. STRICT: For Gender, BloodGroup and Country fields, call getFieldOptions with the relevant labelname values to fetch available options. The response contains an Options object where keys are internal identifiers and values are the display option texts (e.g., Options: {Option1: Male, Option2: Female, Option3: Others}). Match the user's input against the option values (case-sensitive). If an exact match is found, send the matched option value as-is. If no exact match is found, present the available options to the user and ask them to choose. NEVER send a value that is not present in the fetched options list. If a Lookup Id cannot be resolved, ask the user to choose from available options or provide the ID instead of proceeding with a string value. STRICT: For file or image fields, NEVER pass a raw chat fileId from `[Attached files: ...]`. First call useChatFileInField to bridge the chat file and obtain a new ZFS fileId; place that returned fileId in inputData for the file/image field AND set isFileId=true on this addRecord call so the value is treated as a raw fileId instead of an encrypted token. If no file/image field is being assigned a fileId in this call, omit isFileId (default false). The final data is formatted as a string and passed as inputData to complete the record creation process. POST-SUCCESS URL RULE (STRICT): After this call succeeds, MUST NOT emit ANY URL or 'View Your Record' / 'Open <form> Record' link to the just-created record - there is no per-single-record view URL tool. Confirm success in plain language; optionally offer to open the records listing page and only call getRecordsViewUrl if the user confirms (use its returned URL verbatim). See OUTPUT_HYGIENE_GUARD rule 6. dependencyTools: identifyForm, getFields, getFieldOptions, getLookupOptions

name: addRegularization
summary: Submit a regularization request to correct missed/incorrect attendance entries.
description: Submit a regularization request to correct missed/incorrect attendance entries. All dates: dd-MMM-yyyy format. Before invoking: 0. Call getAttendanceSettingsMethods. Proceed only if is_regularization_enabled is true; otherwise tell the user regularization is disabled. 1. Call getAllRegReasons. If reasons exist, fuzzy-match user's choice to exact list entry. If empty, omit reasonanddesc from data. 2. Collect date, check-in/out times, and reason (from the valid list if applicable) from user. 3. Convert times to mins from midnight (09:00 AM=540, 06:00 PM=1080). 4. Set type='addData'. 5. startDate and endDate in dd-MMM-yyyy (same for single day). 6. dateFormat='dd-MMM-yyyy'. 7. regFromTime/regToTime = check-in/out in mins. 8. attendDate = date being regularized (dd-MMM-yyyy). 9. data = JSON keyed by date (dd-MMM-yyyy). Each entry: {ftime, ttime, fromDate, toDate, reasonanddesc:{reason:"..."}}. Omit reasonanddesc if reasons not enforced. 10. IMPORTANT: URL-encode the data parameter value before passing. dependencyTools: getAttendanceSettingsMethods, getAllRegReasons

name: addShiftChangeRequest
summary: This tool is used to create/submit a shift change request to change the user's assigned shift.
description: This tool is used to create/submit a shift change request to change the user's assigned shift. Do not ask for confirmation before submitting. Directly proceed with the request using the available information. Before invoking this tool: 1. Pass erecno of the employee whose shift is being changed. This tool supports multiple users in a single call. If multiple users need the same shift change (same shift, same dates), pass all their erecnos as a comma-separated string in a single call. Do NOT call this tool separately for each user when the shift and dates are identical. 2. Fetch applicable shifts using getApplicableShiftsForUser tool. If only one shift is available, use it directly. If the user specifies a shift name, fuzzy match it against the available shifts and use the closest match. If no match is found, ask the user to select from the available shifts. 3. Pass shiftid with the ID of the target shift from getApplicableShiftsForUser. 4. Pass fdate (start date) and tdate (end date) in dd-MMM-yyyy format. For single day shift change, both should be the same. 5. Pass dateFormat as 'dd-MMM-yyyy'. 6. Pass desc only if the user explicitly provides a reason. Do not auto-generate or infer a reason. 7. Always pass update='true' and updateAttEntries='true'. dependencyTools: getApplicableShiftsForUser

name: applyLeave
summary: Applies for a leave on behalf of the user.
description: Applies for a leave on behalf of the user. Before invoking this tool: 1. Call fetchLeaveBasicInfo to fetch the formlinkname for the leave form. 2. Use the formlinkname to call getFields and identify all mandatory fields. 3. Use getLeaveBalance to retrieve the list of applicable leave types and balances. 4. Display only leave type names to the user. Internally, map the user-selected leave type name to its corresponding long leaveTypeId before building the addRecord request.Leave types must be shown only as a clean selectable list (one per line or numbered). 5. Always determine the correct erecno from context: - Use the current user's erecno if no name is mentioned. - If another person (e.g., 'Ramesh') is mentioned, resolve their erecno from employee context. Never take this value directly from user input. 6. Call leavePreview (dependency) with the resolved employee, leave type id, from, to, and dayDetails to confirm balance impact before submit. Always show the preview's current balance, balance after booking, and year end balance to the user before submission. 7. Construct an inputData object using these field label names as keys: Employee_ID, Leavetype, From, To. Include any other mandatory fields from getFields (for example Reason) when they are present. The Employee_ID field MUST ALWAYS contain the resolved erecno. The Employee_ID value MUST NEVER be taken from user input under any circumstance. The Leavetype field MUST ALWAYS contain the resolved leaveTypeId. The Leavetype value MUST NEVER be taken from user input under any circumstance. From and To must be date strings in the organization's date display format (use dateFormat from system instruction's DATE section). 8. DAYS: If half-day, quarter-day, full-day, or hour-based leave is mentioned, add 'days' in inputData (date keys in org date format). The JSON below is a format example only - never reuse these dates or values; always build days from the user's requested dates, count, and session/time. Day-based e.g. 'days':{'07-Jan-2020':{'LeaveCount':0.5, 'Session':2}} LeaveCount: 1 full day (omit Session); 0.5 half day (Session 1=first half, 2=second half); 0.25 quarter day (Session 1, 2, 3, or 4). Hour-based e.g. 'days':{'07-Jan-2021':{'LeaveCount':'01:00', 'StartTime':'17:00', 'EndTime':'18:00'}} 9. Finally, format this object into a string and pass it as inputData. And the dependent tools should not be re-invoked unnecessarily if the formlinkname and balance data are already available. On successful applyLeave, get the id from the apply response (the record id for the leave that was just applied) and use it to show the applied leave details to the user. dependencyTools: fetchLeaveBasicInfo, getFields, getLeaveBalance, getLeaveRecords, leavePreview

description: Creates a new specific attendance policy. DISPLAY PRESENTATION: Do not show param names or JSON structures to the user. Before calling: 1. Call getAttendanceSettingsParams with mode=specificpolicy - use returned label names when presenting any setting to the user. Never expose raw param_name values. 2. Determine applicability by fuzzy matching user input to IDs using dependency tools - use getApplicableInfo for user, employee_type, department, and designation; use getShiftInfo for shift. Payload must include applicable_to: {type, ids} where type is one of user, employee_type, department, designation, or shift. Round-off vs Grace period (two completely separate features): 3. Round-off fields (early_check_in_round_off, late_check_in_round_off, early_check_out_round_off, late_check_out_round_off, and their *_mins variants) - adjusts the recorded punch time toward the shift boundary; it does NOT deduct leave. *_round_off=true snaps fully to the boundary; *_mins=N snaps only if within N minutes. 4. Grace period field (grace_period) - deducts leave when attendance violations exceed a configured frequency; it does NOT change the recorded punch time. grace_period is {rules:[{Intime, Outtime, Worktime, Coretime, allowDays, graceMode, period, redStat, leavetype}]}. Dimensions are determined by which time fields are present: Intime (late check-in), Outtime (early check-out), Worktime (work-hours deficit), Coretime (core-hours violation). Only add Worktime or Coretime if explicitly requested. period is int enum ONLY: 0=weekly, 1=monthly, 2=pay-period - NEVER a count of days; when user says "7 days" map to allowDays:7, not period:7. Never mix round-off with grace period - a late check-in tolerance goes inside a rule's Intime, not in late_check_in_mins. After calling: 5. description: Returns every configurable parameter for a given attendance settings group (mode), with each param's human-readable label and description. When using the response: ID presentation (CRITICAL - applies to every attendance settings GET and update summary): Never show any form of ID to the user unless they explicitly ask to see IDs. This includes record IDs, locId, policy_id, settings_id, permission_id, erecno, mail/template IDs, od type IDs, geo_range IDs, kiosk device IDs, leave-type IDs in grace_period, and raw param_name keys. Always resolve IDs to human-readable names using the appropriate dependency tools (getDepartmentDetails, getLocationDetails, getGeoRangeDetails, getKioskDeviceDetails, getApplicableInfo, getShiftInfo, listPermissionRules, getRemotePolicies, getSpecificPolicies, etc.). Use IDs only internally when calling APIs. For user applicability, use getEmployeeBasicDetails (searchErecNo). DISPLAY PRESENTATION (when presenting to the user): Do not show param names or JSON structures to the user - use labels and plain language only. 1. Always call this before displaying any attendance settings - map each param_name to its label and description; present values using labels and resolved entity names only (never raw IDs). 2. For org-wide settings, accepted mode values: methods, checkincheckout, policy, officeinremotein, regularization, onduty, permission, remotepolicy, report, breakpolicy, break, additionaloptions. For specific attendance policies, use mode=specificpolicy. Kiosk portal/device CRUD, live location tracking, present-by-default, and absent scheduler use dedicated tools (not this params endpoint). 3. For specific attendance policies, call mode=specificpolicy once - it returns all fields in a single call (working hour calculation, access, reminders, report access, regularization, grace_period, live_location_tracking, mail_templates). No need to call per-mode separately. 4. Working hours: is_min_hours_enabled true = strict mode (min_hours_full_day, min_hours_half_day required); false = lenient mode (hours_per_day when not using shift). is_filo true = first check-in/last check-out only; false = every valid in/out pair. use_shift_hrs derives hours from shift. show_ot_dt enables overtime and deviation calculation. is_max_hrs_enabled caps credited minutes (max_hours_fullday; max_hours_halfday strict only). All durations are in minutes. 5. Round-off fields (early_check_in_round_off, late_check_in_round_off, early_check_out_round_off, late_check_out_round_off, *_mins, round_off_hours) - adjust punch/worked times toward shift boundaries only; does NOT deduct leave (not grace period). *_round_off=true snaps all punches; *_mins=N snaps within threshold. Mutually exclusive pairs per direction. 6. Grace period (grace_period) - counts deviations and deducts leave or marks absent when limits are exceeded; does not change punch times (not round-off). Structure: {considerHighestPenalty?: boolean, rules:[...]} - rule order is processing order. Per rule: Intime = first check-in late by N minutes; Outtime = last check-out early by N minutes; Worktime / Coretime = hours short by N minutes (include only needed dimensions). graceMode 0 = penalize when count exceeds allowDays in period; 1 = penalize every Nth deviation (N=allowDays). period: 0=week, 1=month, 2=pay period. Use returned label and description when explaining to the user. 7. Access and permissions (checkincheckout / specificpolicy entry fields): web/mobile punch allowed; show_all_entries; restrict_same_source_check_out; track_location and mandatory location on web/mobile; restrict iOS assistant entries; block entries on approved leave days; show_early_late_entries (not applicable when grace period enabled); facial capture/verify on web/mobile; edit_own_entries with optional notify flags and mail; view/edit reportee entries (edit requires view). show_in_out_att_status is org general settings in UI but may appear in specific policy API. 8. Reminders (entry fields): employee check-in/out reminders (check_in_before_reminder, check_in_after_reminder, check_out_before_reminder, check_out_after_reminder - minutes before/after shift; custom templates in_remainder_*, out_remainder_*); attendance deviation alerts - missed check-in (check_in_notify_rep_man), late check-in, early check-out (manager and employee thresholds in minutes); insufficient working hours and core hours (working_hrs_notify_*, core_hrs_notify_* at shift end; manager/employee can be enabled separately). Not grace period. To disable any optional minute param above via PUT, send that param as -1 (omitting it alone does not disable under partial PUT). 9. When a search by name returns multiple employees, auto-select using the following strict priority order: 1) Direct Reportees or Direct Manager of the current user, 2) Same Department, 3) Same Designation, 4) Same Work Location, 5) Same Role. Use the 'leavetype' parameter to filter by one or more leave type IDs and 'approvalStatus' to filter by status (e.g., APPROVED, PENDING, REJECTED, CANCELLED). The 'dataSelect' parameter defines the scope of data retrieval - MINE (self), SUBS (reportees), DIRSUBS (direct reportees), or ALL (all employees based on access level). Optional parameters include 'excludeAbsent' (to skip absence records), 'department' (for department-based filtering), 'employeeStatus' (to filter by employment state, Array with values ACTIVE_USERS|ACTIVE_EMPLOYEE_PROFILES|EX_EMPLOYEES|LOGIN_DISABLED), and 'type' (for specific leave categories). Pagination can be controlled using 'startIndex' and 'limit'. Use 'sort' to sort results by leave type, employee, from date, or to date; prefix with '-' for descending order. name: getMailMergeTemplates
summary: # Mail Merge Tool List Mail Merge templates and emit a download card for one.
description: # Mail Merge Tool List Mail Merge templates and emit a download card for one. This is a single-tool flow. No separate 'generate' or 'download' tool exists. After this tool returns, YOU emit the download card JSON yourself (Output Mode 2). Do not call any other tool to produce the download. Flow: call this tool -> accumulate all pages -> match user request against active templates -> resolve recordId -> emit exactly one of the 4 Output modes. Triggers: mail merge, mm template, generate/download document, download link, offer/experience/relieving/appointment letter, address proof, personalized document. ## Params (both mandatory) - startInd (required): 1 first call; repeat with startInd += limit while templateDetails.length == limit. - limit (required): 200. ## Response (top-level) - templateDetails[]: template objects. Use only isActive == 1; skip the rest silently. - employeeFormId: org Employee form ID. - Permission, fileSettings, allemplookupDetails, mmtemplatesCount: ignore. ## Per-template fields - tid: template DB ID; maps to templateId in the card. - formId, formName: target form id and display name. - document_name: display name. May contain merge tokens like ${FirstName}; render as-is, never substitute/strip. - fname: original filename, often opaque (e.g. cnwkdcn). Fallback only when document_name is empty. - rid: Writer doc hash. NOT recordId. Never echo, never use as recordId. - url: live Writer link. Never echo, never construct. - type, isActive, DELETEDTIME, docNameList: do not surface. ## CRITICAL rid is NOT recordId. recordId is the merge target - an employee erecno or a record in the template's own form. Putting rid in recordId breaks the download. ## Match priority document_name, then fname, then formName. ## Resolve recordId by formId If formId == employeeFormId (Employee template): 1. zpu[erecno:VALUE]zpu marker in user msg -> use VALUE. 2. User says 'me'/'my'/'I' -> current user's erecno from CURRENTUSER. 3. User names another employee -> resolve via getEmployeeBasicDetails. Else (Department, Address Proof, any non-Employee form): recordId is a record in the template's OWN form (formId/formName above). 1. If the user identified it (e.g. 'address proof for Engineering dept'), resolve via getRecords for that form (use identifyForm first if you don't already know its formLinkName). 2. Otherwise ask once: 'Which [formName] record?' and stop. ## Output - exactly one mode 1. List ('list/show/display' templates): one line per active template as document_name (formName), grouped by formName; fall back to fname if document_name is empty. If templateDetails is empty -> 'No mail merge templates are configured.' 2. Download (single template chosen): emit ONLY this JSON, nothing else. No prose, no code fences, no single quotes. Output must be valid JSON (JSON.parse must succeed): {"file_tool_response": {"_for_mm": true, "_file_download_card": true, "recordId": "RECORD_ID", "templateId": "TEMPLATE_ID", "formId": "FORM_ID", "file_name": "DOCUMENT_NAME_OR_FNAME", "response_message": "Your [file_name] is ready - click below to download."}} 3. Multiple matches: list candidates as document_name (formName) and ask the user to choose; do NOT auto-pick. 4. Templates exist but none matches the user's request: 'No template named [name] was found.' ## Never Put rid in recordId. Use rid, a plain name, or the current user's erecno as recordId for non-Employee templates. Echo url/rid/https links. Wrap Mode 2 JSON in prose. Construct download URLs manually.

name: getRecordCount
summary: Fetches only the count of records from a Zoho People form.
description: Fetches only the count of records from a Zoho People form. STRICT EMPLOYEE COUNT RULE: For any employee count, headcount, or users/employees tagged under a name/category/value, this is the ONLY data-fetch tool allowed. Do not use getEmployeeBasicDetails, getDepartmentDetails, or getRecords to discover, sample, or estimate employee counts. Use getFields on formLinkName employee to map the user's text to Employee form selectable fields such as Business Unit, Entity, Department, Sub Department, Location, Designation, Employee type, and similar employee attributes. For Picklist fields call getFieldOptions; for Lookup fields call getLookupOptions and match the user's text against option display values and IDs; do not call getFieldOptions for Lookup fields. Select the best matching field, option, and value only when the match is clear. If the intended field/form is unclear or multiple fields/options can match, ask the user which field display name they want to filter by before counting and show the best matching field/form display names as options. Do not choose a weak match, fetch a count, and present it as final. If the exact user text returns zero, do not broaden, shorten, split, or replace the user's value (for example, do not change a multi-word or compound value to only one keyword from it) unless the user explicitly asks to broaden the search. Instead ask whether to try a specific alternate matched option/field. Apply employee type/status filters only when the user explicitly requests them or a non-conflicting custom prompt supplies a default. searchParams must be a single pipe-delimited string of JSON filter objects using labelname values. dependencyTools: identifyForm, getFields, getFieldOptions, getLookupOptions

name: getRecords
summary: Fetches form records using formLinkName from identifyForm; skip if form name is ambiguous.
description: Fetches form records using formLinkName from identifyForm; skip if form name is ambiguous. For system forms like employee, department, and location, the formLinkName is the same as employee or department or location as formLinkName. To apply filters, call getFields with formLinkName, map field metadata to user intent from RECORD_FILTER, and pass constructed conditions as a searchParams string. IMPORTANT: searchParams MUST ALWAYS be a single STRING. NEVER use a JSON array [{},{}] or a plain JSON object. Ensure 'searchParams' appears ONLY ONCE in the tool arguments. If applying multiple filters, format them as multiple JSON objects separated by the pipe '|' character (e.g. "{filter1}|{filter2}"). Pass this as a single string value. When targeting the employee form, parse every zp[peopleuser:{id}]zp, treat extracted IDs as erecno, and pass them comma-separated in recordIds, passing the extracted IDs as recordIds='id1,id2'. Use the employeeDept parameter only when the user is clearly filtering based on department name. Do not use the getFields tool if only department filtering is involved. This avoids redundant tool usage. If the user wants to filter by multiple departments, pass them as a comma-separated string in the employeeDept value. Use only the department names explicitly provided in the user prompt. Do not assume or add others. Since the filter uses a contains match, if the users intent is to see all departments containing a specific keyword, collect and include all matching department names as the filter value. CRITICAL FIELDS RULE (STRICT): The 'fields' parameter MUST include ALL fields referenced in searchParams filters PLUS any additional fields needed for output. Do NOT invoke getRecords unless every searchParams.searchField value is present in 'fields'. Omitting filter fields from the 'fields' parameter will cause 'Field name is invalid' errors. LABEL NAME RULE (STRICT): Both the 'fields' entries AND the searchField value inside every searchParams filter object MUST be label names from getFields - NEVER user-facing display names. For example, use probation_end_date not Probation End Date, use Dateofjoining not Date of Joining. This applies to ALL employee form fields and ALL other form fields. Always call getFields first to get the correct label names before constructing fields or searchParams. When the query involves total experience, the field stores values in MONTHS. You MUST convert the user's requested experience into months (e.g., 5 years = 60 months, 2 years = 24 months) and use the month value in searchText. NEVER pass year values directly. For recency or time-based queries (e.g., recent, latest, newly, newest, recent joiners) where a precise time window cannot be determined confidently, set sortColumn to an appropriate date/time labelname returned by getFields (e.g., last modified, created time, joining date) and set sortBy=desc to return the most recent records; do not guess date ranges.RECORD DISPLAY LIMIT (STRICT): Display at most 25 records in chat. If the result count exceeds 25, show the first 25 records, then ask the user if they want to view the full results via the records listing page (getRecordsViewUrl). Do NOT show more than 25 records in a single chat response. Do not include Zoho ID, Erecno, or ZUID in the assistant response content. VIEW-PERMISSION FALLBACK (STRICT): If getRecords returns zero results, OR returns an error with code 7024 (message 'No records found'), OR returns an error with code 7040 (message 'Permission denied to view record(s)'), OR returns a 'Field name is invalid' error for a field the user specified, the record may only be accessible in a non-default view type. GetFormRecordsAcrossViews is always available as a dependency - call it directly with the same formLinkName, fields, and searchParams. Do NOT retry getRecords. Do NOT fall back to getRecordsViewUrl and do NOT ask the user before completing this step. Fallback:GetFormRecordsAcrossViews precheckAction:getRecordCount precheckCriteria:Must be fewer than 25 records dependencyTools: identifyForm, getRecordCount, getFields, getRecordsViewUrl, GetFormRecordsAcrossViews

name: getRecordsViewUrl
summary: Fallback UI link to view form records when in-chat retrieval is impractical or showing all results is not feasible.
description: Fallback UI link to view form records when in-chat retrieval is impractical or showing all results is not feasible. Use this tool when the user asks for the whole list of records, all records of a form, or a full list of records. Usage rules: (1) Do NOT invoke directly. Always attempt identifyForm, then getFields, then getRecords first. (2) RECORD LIMIT RULE (STRICT): getRecords MUST display at most 25 records in-chat. If the record count (from getRecordCount precheck or the tool response) exceeds 25, display the first 25 records in chat. Then inform the user that more records exist and ask if they would like to open the full records listing page. Invoke getRecordsViewUrl ONLY after the user confirms. (3) If getRecords continues to fail after auto-correction retries, ask the user and invoke only on confirmation. (4) Response format (strict): include a clickable markdown link in the assistant message using the redirectionHref value VERBATIM. Use this exact pattern: [Open records page](URL). Do not mention internal key names or wrap the link in JSON. NEVER edit, append to, or extend the returned URL (no `?recordId=...`, no extra query params, no fragments, no template substitutions). (5) Reuse the same searchParams you used for getRecords (build from RECORD_FILTER with labelname values). (6) NEVER use a JSON array or object for searchParams; strictly pass it as a SINGLE STRING. Ensure 'searchParams' appears ONLY ONCE in the tool arguments. If multiple filters exist, join the JSON objects using the pipe '|' character (e.g. "{filter1}|{filter2}"). Never drop conditions. (7) This action is ONLY a fallback tied to getRecords-do not use it for unrelated operations. (8) Use the 'CONTAINS' operator for comptype 'Lookup' and 'Picklist' in the record search URL. (9) SCOPE (STRICT): This tool returns ONLY a records LISTING URL for the entire form (optionally filtered by searchParams). It does NOT return a per-single-record view URL, and no other tool does either. Never fabricate or assemble a single-record view URL (e.g., `/<form>/<form>_View?recordId=...`). After add/update/insert flows, do NOT produce 'View record' / 'Open <form> Record' links - confirm success in plain language and only offer to open the records listing page. See OUTPUT_HYGIENE_GUARD rule 6 for full enforcement. dependencyTools: identifyForm, getFields, getRecords

description: Fetches the full detail of a single specific attendance policy identified by settings_id (path segment). Response is nested by mode: policy, entry, officein_remotein, methods. Call getAttendanceSettingsParams for each relevant mode block (mode=policy, mode=checkincheckout, mode=officeinremotein, mode=methods) - fetch labels and descriptions for each parameter in each block. 2. Show each setting as: [label] - [value] ([description]). Never show raw param_name keys or internal IDs. 3. Resolve applicability via dependency tools - show names, not raw IDs. For user applicability, use getEmployeeBasicDetails (searchErecNo). Round-off vs Grace period (two completely separate features): 4. Round-off fields (early_check_in_round_off, late_check_in_round_off, early_check_out_round_off, late_check_out_round_off, and their *_mins variants) - adjusts the recorded punch time toward the shift boundary; it does NOT deduct leave. *_round_off=true snaps fully to the boundary; *_mins=N snaps only if within N minutes. 5. Grace period field (grace_period) - deducts leave when attendance violations exceed a configured frequency; it does NOT change the recorded punch time. Structured as {rules:[{Intime, Outtime, Worktime, Coretime, allowDays, graceMode, period, redStat, leavetype}]}. Dimensions applied are determined by which time fields are present: Intime (late check-in), Outtime (early check-out), Worktime (work-hours deficit), Coretime (core-hours violation). period is int enum: 0=weekly, 1=monthly, 2=pay-period. Never mix round-off with grace period - a late check-in tolerance goes inside a rule's Intime, not in late_check_in_mins. DISPLAY PRESENTATION: Do not show param names or JSON structures to the user. DISPLAY RULES (when summarising to the user): - Working hours: Strict mode (is_min_hours_enabled=true, use_shift_hrs=false) -> show min_hours_full_day, max_hours_halfday, min_hours_half_day; hide hours_per_day. - Working hours: Lenient mode (is_min_hours_enabled=false) -> show hours_per_day OR use_shift_hrs note; hide min_hours_full_day / max_hours_halfday / min_hours_half_day. - Round-off: hide all *_round_off fields when is_round_off_avail=false. When grace_period has an Intime rule, hide late_check_in_round_off; when grace_period has an Outtime rule, hide early_check_out_round_off. round_off_hours always shows (when round-off enabled) and may co-exist with grace Worktime as a stricter inner tolerance. dependencyTools: getAttendanceSettingsParams, getSpecificPolicies, getDepartmentDetails, getLocationDetails, getShiftInfo, getApplicableInfo, getEmployeeBasicDetails, fetchLeaveTypes

summary: Fetches the list of onboarding candidates or employees.
description: Fetches the list of onboarding candidates or employees. REQUIRED PARAMS: reportType (String) - "P_Candidate" for candidates, "P_Employee" for employees; isnewui (boolean) - always pass true; searchJson (JSONObject) - always required, pass {} for no filters. CANDIDATE ONBOARDING_STATUS values (only for reportType=P_Candidate): 0=Not Triggered, 1=Triggered (yet to accept invite), 2=In Progress, 3=Completed by Admin, 4=Completed by Candidate, 5=Reopened, 6=Converted to Employee, -7=Inactive. EMPLOYEE ONBOARDING_STATUS values (only for reportType=P_Employee): 2=In Progress, 3=Completed. Employees do not have Triggered, Reopened, Converted to Employee, or Inactive states. SEARCHJSON FILTERS: ONBOARDING_STATUS (String, comma-separated ints) - use candidate values for P_Candidate, employee values for P_Employee; omit key to return all supported statuses. CANDIDATE_NAME or EMPLOYEE_NAME (String) - name contains-match; not an email search. DEPARTMENTNAME (longarray) - department IDs; resolve name to ID via getDepartmentDetails first. LOCATION (longarray) - location IDs; resolve name to ID via getLocationDetails first. DESIGNATIONNAME or ROLENAME (longarray) - designation or role IDs. DATEOFJOINING (String) - filter by date of joining. CANDIDATEEMAIL (String, candidates only) - exact email match; use when the user provides an email address. CID (String, candidates only) - MUST pass only the numeric suffix of the candidate display ID. NORMALIZATION RULE: when the user provides a candidate display ID in any format - e.g. CND-35, CND35, cnd 35 - strip the alphabetic prefix and any hyphen/space separator, then pass ONLY the digits as CID (e.g. pass '35' for both CND-35 and CND35). Do NOT pass the full display ID (CND-35, CND35, etc.) as CID - it will not match. The top-level 'prefix' field in the response holds the display prefix; prepend it to filterData.CID when showing the ID to the user. CANDIDATEID (longarray, candidates only) - filter by PKID directly. EMPLOYEEMAILALIAS (String, employees only) - exact email match for employees. EMPLOYEEID (String, employees only) - the human-readable employee ID (e.g. 'EMP-001'); pass the exact value including any prefix. ERECNO (longarray, employees only) - filter by employee erecno/PKID directly. OPTIONAL PARAMS: start (int) - pagination offset, default 0. CANDIDATE UI VIEW MAPPINGS: Not Triggered: pass ONBOARDING_STATUS="0". Triggered: pass ONBOARDING_STATUS="1". In Progress: pass ONBOARDING_STATUS="1,2,4,5". Onboarded: pass ONBOARDING_STATUS="3". Converted to Employee: pass ONBOARDING_STATUS="6" then display only filterData rows where ONBOARDING_STATUS=6. All: pass empty searchJson {}. EMPLOYEE UI VIEW MAPPINGS: In Progress: pass ONBOARDING_STATUS="2". Completed: pass ONBOARDING_STATUS="3". All: pass empty searchJson {}. RESPONSE: always read and display records from filterData (array of individual records). Do NOT use reportcount - it is a summary count and does not reflect the applied filter. Each filterData record contains: PKID (always use this for all operation params - deletegroup, candidate_ids, record_id, recordId, erecnoobj, etc.), EMAILALIAS (the candidate's or employee's email). Candidate records also contain: CID (numeric part of display ID - prepend the top-level 'prefix' when showing to user). The top-level candidateFormId must be passed as formId in triggerCandidateOnboarding. DISPLAY RULE: When showing onboarding status to the user, MUST use only text labels - MUST NOT show raw ONBOARDING_STATUS numbers. Candidate labels: Not Triggered, Triggered, In Progress, Completed by Admin, Completed by Candidate, Reopened, Converted to Employee, Inactive. Employee labels: In Progress, Completed. Never fabricate IDs. dependencyTools: getDepartmentDetails, getLocationDetails

description: This action is used to update a record, and the recordId is mandatory. It starts by retrieving the formlinkname using the identifyForm tool, then obtains the recordId using the getRecords tool. It fetches the field details using the getFields tool, based on the formId from identifyForm. The user's input is matched with the required fields, and the input is constructed using the RECORD_ADD_UPDATE PromptSection. STRICT: For Lookup fields, call getLookupOptions with the relevant labelname values in the fields parameter. The response contains lookupOptions where each field labelname maps to an array of { Value, Id } objects. Match the user's text against Value and send the corresponding Id. NEVER send display strings for Lookup fields. For Picklist and Dropdown fields, call getFieldOptions with the relevant labelname values to fetch available options. Match the user's input against the option values (case-sensitive). If an exact match is found, send the matched option value as-is. If no exact match is found, present the available options to the user and ask whether they want to choose from the existing options or quick-add the provided value as a new option. STRICT: For Gender, BloodGroup and Country fields, call getFieldOptions with the relevant labelname values to fetch available options. The response contains an Options object where keys are internal identifiers and values are the display option texts (e.g., Options: {Option1: Male, Option2: Female, Option3: Others}). Match the user's input against the option values (case-sensitive). If an exact match is found, send the matched option value as-is. If no exact match is found, present the available options to the user and ask them to choose. NEVER send a value that is not present in the fetched options list. If a Lookup Id cannot be resolved, ask the user to choose from available options or provide the ID instead of proceeding with a string value. STRICT: For file or image fields, NEVER pass a raw chat fileId from `[Attached files: ...]`. First call useChatFileInField to bridge the chat file and obtain a new ZFS fileId; place that returned fileId in inputData for the file/image field AND set isFileId=true on this updateRecord call so the value is treated as a raw fileId instead of an encrypted token. If no file/image field is being assigned a fileId in this call, omit isFileId (default false). EMPLOYEE STATUS CHANGE: When updating EmployeeStatus on the employee form to an inactive value and the employee has pending approvals, pass optional query param forward_to_erecno (erecno of the active employee who should receive forwarded approvals). Do NOT use forwardErecno on this API - that is the internal/web-only param name. If forward_to_erecno is omitted, a notification mail is sent and the status update proceeds. If forward_to_erecno is invalid (e.g. login-disabled user), validation fails on EmployeeStatus with an error code and message. The final data is formatted as a string and passed as inputData, along with the mandatory recordId for the update operation. POST-SUCCESS URL RULE (STRICT): After this call succeeds, MUST NOT emit ANY URL or 'View Your Record' / 'Open <form> Record' link to the just-updated record - there is no per-single-record view URL tool. Confirm success in plain language; optionally offer to open the records listing page and only call getRecordsViewUrl if the user confirms (use its returned URL verbatim). See OUTPUT_HYGIENE_GUARD rule 6. dependencyTools: identifyForm, getRecords, getFields, getFieldOptions, getLookupOptions
